messages:
Liam (docs): Hey team, PR #4381 is blocked by CI/docs preview. The model routing example in the migration guide shows `route: 'by_region'` taking precedence over `fallback`, but runtime says fallback wins in some cases. Need a clear rule to document.

qa-bot: Deploy preview 4381 - build failed. Error: Example test failed (example-routing-snippet.js). Linkcheck: broken anchor /guides/migration#routing-priority (404). Logs: https://deploy.example/4381/logs

Priya (sdk): Which SDK snippet are you using? We changed the JS helper in @redwood/sdk v1.5.0: routing helpers now surface the server decision tree differently. If the snippet uses legacy helper `client.routeRequest(...)` it may show the old order.

Liam (docs): It's using the helper. I copied it from the old migration guide to be explicit about precedence. The snippet currently:

```js
const res = await client.routeRequest({
  model: 'rwd-medium',
  route: 'by_region',
  fallback: ['nearby_pool', 'standard_pool']
})
```

And the comment says "route > fallback".

Jas (platform): Runtime behavior: routing policy says we try explicit route target first; if that target is healthy but has no compatible model variant, we then evaluate fallbacks. However, when a 'sticky' routing cookie is present (sticky=true) and the sticky target is unhealthy we immediately skip to fallback. The docs need to call out the sticky case.

Omar (prod-eng): Also note Dedicated deployments with older config may not have the sticky feature enabled. So precedence can differ: Hosted(default) = route -> fallback (unless sticky=false edge cases). Legacy Dedicated = sometimes fallback first for certain load-shedding configs. It's messy.

Priya (sdk): SDK now exposes `routingDecision` metadata on responses for clarity. Recommend example show how to inspect that instead of asserting a strict precedence. Example:

```js
const res = await client.generate({ model: 'rwd-medium', prompt })
console.log(res.routingDecision) // { chosen: 'nearby_pool', reason: 'route-unavailable' }
```

Liam (docs): OK we can change the text to "Routing decisions are environment-dependent; inspect response.routingDecision for the final decision" and update the snippet to use generate + log metadata. That should avoid the hard claim.

Jas (platform): Please add a tiny section listing common variations: hosted standard, new Dedicated, legacy Dedicated. Make it one-paragraph with bulletish lines.

Liam (docs): Will do. Question for Priya: should example pin the SDK version in the snippet to v1.5.2? Current docs site was on 1.4.8.

Priya (sdk): Yes pin to 1.5.2 and use the new metadata property. Also update the example test harness name from example-routing-snippet.js -> example-routing-snippet-v1_5.js to avoid CI flakiness.

Omar (prod-eng): One more edge: when model variant matching fails but `allow_fallback_model_family=true` is set at the project level, runtime may map to a lower-tier family automatically. Document that as an opt-in behavior.

Liam (docs): Got it. I'll: 1) update snippet to generate+inspect routingDecision, 2) pin SDK to 1.5.2, 3) add short paragraph about hosted/new Dedicated/legacy Dedicated differences, 4) mention allow_fallback_model_family opt-in. Pushing changes in ~30m.

qa-bot: Build queued for deploy-preview 4382.

Priya (sdk): Ping me after you push so I can sanity-check the snippet. If CI still complains about link anchor, Maya (runtime/docs site) probably renamed the heading id.

Liam (docs): Will ping. Thanks all.

qa-bot: Deploy preview 4382 - success. Linkcheck fixed.

Priya (sdk): Quick review done, looks good to me.

Omar (prod-eng): LGTM from my side.

Liam (docs): @Jas can you give final signoff on the hosted vs dedicated wording?

Jas (platform): LGTM, minor nit: change "legacy Dedicated" -> "legacy Dedicated pools". Approve when you update that line.

Liam (docs): Fixed and merged. Thanks everyone :tada:
